Alex — really appreciate the clear list. Post-call recap and next steps below so we have alignment. Attaching a short SLO qualification form and an autoscale behavior diagram for reference.

Summary (post-call):
- Goal: validate that Redwood can meet FastPay p50 / p95 latency targets for both hosted and Dedicated/private deployments, and to size warm pool / burst capacity for traffic spikes.
- Info we need from you (suggested inputs on the attached form): p50/p95 targets, typical message length (tokens), percent of streaming vs non-streaming calls, desired concurrency (peak and steady), and acceptable scale-up windows.

Quick answers from our side:
- Hosted API: typical p50 ~ 30-80ms for lightweight models; p95 depends on sequence length and batching but we can often provide p95 < 300ms with recommended batching and prefix caching.
- Dedicated: more predictable p95 (often < 200–250ms) with pinned capacity and warm pools.
- Streaming: streaming itself doesn't prevent autoscaling, but it affects how we manage warm pools and idle vs active connections. Long-lived streaming sessions benefit from pre-warmed workers.
- Scale-up: cold start to fully-warmed for a new model/pool is highly dependent on model size and node type; warm pool instances can be kept idle-ready (seconds-level readiness) but spinning new GPUs from zero can take minutes.

Proposed next steps:
1) Please complete the attached SLO_Qualification_Form.pdf with p50/p95, token distribution, expected percent streaming, and steady/peak concurrency.
2) We'll produce a tailored Mutual Action Plan with a Dedicated capacity recommendation and proposed warm-pool configuration.
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive to review autoscale behavior and test scenarios (Rishi will propose an availability window).

I attached: SLO_Qualification_Form.pdf, autoscale-diagram.png.

If you can return the filled form by Tue 20 Apr, we can get the MAP and draft quote over same week.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Marissa Cole

Marissa — filling this out inline for speed; I'll upload the completed PDF shortly. Answers below:

- p50 target: <= 100ms for user-facing inference (text-gen short prompts).
- p95 target: <= 300ms for user-facing; for background batch tasks p95 <= 1s acceptable.
- Typical prompt size: 60–120 tokens; some long-form generation up to 800 tokens (~10% of calls).
- Percent streaming: ~25% of user-facing calls require streaming.
- Steady-state concurrency (avg): 150–200 concurrent requests.
- Peak concurrency: up to 450 concurrent during promotions.
- Steady throughput: ~120–160 req/s; burst up to 700–900 req/s for short windows (1–3 minutes).
- Desired scale-up window: prefer < 90s to recover to 80% capacity; for guaranteed levels we can consider pre-warmed pools.

Notes: We want autoscaling behavior that minimizes queueing for user-facing traffic. For streaming sessions, preserving connection stability is important; dropped streams are unacceptable.

—Alex

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: FastPay mutual action plan & capacity proposal

Thanks for the details, Alex — helpful and clear. Putting a proposed MAP and technical notes here so FastPay and your infra team have a concrete starting point.

High-level proposal (draft):
- Deployment: Dedicated capacity with a mixed warm-pool strategy (small always-warm worker set + burstable pool for short spikes).
- Warm pools: keep ~20–30% of expected peak concurrency pre-warmed (we recommend ~120 warm workers based on your peak). Warm workers respond in seconds.
- Burstable pool: additional workers that can spin up in ~60–180s depending on node provisioning; we can reduce spin-up time by using pre-baked images and thin model loading.
- Queueing: we will prioritize user-facing streaming requests and surface queueing metrics; recommend soft-queue thresholds + graceful degradation to a smaller model variant for non-critical calls.
- SLA/guardrails: for guaranteed <90s recovery we suggest committing to a minimum reserved capacity for promotion windows.

Action items and owners:
- FastPay: confirm whether you want a hard SLA on <90s warm-up (finance/legal will need to sign off). (Alex)
- Redwood: prepare MAP doc and cost estimate for Dedicated+warm-pool config. (Rishi)
- Schedule tech deep-dive (Marissa/Rishi) — propose Wed 28 Apr 10am PT or Thu 29 Apr 9am PT.

I'll attach a short diagram of the warm-pool flow (see autoscale-diagram.png) and a draft cost model offline.

-Rishi
